# SAUTI

Your AI, Your World.

An AI assistant interface for African users: ask a question in English, Swahili
or French and get back answers, marketplace listings, explanations and news.

## Stack

| Concern | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Framework | Next.js 15 (App Router) |
| Language | TypeScript, strict mode |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS 3.4 |
| Backend | Flask (`backend/`), reached over HTTP |
| Icons | `lucide-react` |
| Class merging | `clsx` + `tailwind-merge` |
| Component variants | `class-variance-authority` |

**This frontend talks to the real backend.** Answers are generated by the
configured language model, and listings, articles, popular searches and
languages all come from live endpoints. Nothing on screen is sample data.

## Getting started

Two terminals. The backend first:

```bash
# from the repository root
pip install -e .
FLASK_APP=wsgi.py python -m flask run --port 8000
```

Then the frontend:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).

The backend needs a provider key to answer questions. Put it in `.env` at the
repository root:

```
GROQ_API_KEY=...        # the model provider
GROQ_MODEL=...          # optional, has a default
ADMIN_TOKEN=...         # required only for the admin routes
```

Without a key the backend still boots and serves the marketplace and news
endpoints, but chat requests fall back to a deterministic offline reply.
`/settings` shows live engine status, so you can tell which mode you are in.

## Data flow

`lib/api.ts` is the single seam between the UI and the backend. Every function
maps to exactly one Flask route and its return type mirrors the JSON that route
actually emits.

| Screen | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Hero, Internet, Education | `POST /api/sauti/chat` |
| Hero mic | `POST /api/sauti/transcribe` |
| Business | `POST /api/marketplace/search` |
| News | `GET /api/marketplace/news` |
| Popular searches | `GET /api/marketplace/popular` |
| Saved | `GET/POST /api/marketplace/saved` |
| History | `GET /api/chat/history/<id>` |
| Settings | `GET /api/health`, `/api/sauti/health`, `/api/languages` |

Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` to point at a backend other than
`http://localhost:8000`.

### Reading a response correctly

`engine` names the **configured** provider, so it reads `"groq"` whether or not
groq answered. Use the outcome fields instead:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `engine_ok` | `true` only when the model generated the reply |
| `degraded` | `true` whenever the reply is not a live answer |
| `engine_error` | Short safe reason; never contains provider internals |

A degraded turn renders with an explicit notice rather than being passed off as
a real answer.

### Model replies

Answers come back as markdown. `lib/richText.tsx` renders the subset the model
actually uses — headings, bullets, numbered lists, bold, italic, inline code —
as React elements. It never builds HTML strings, so a reply containing markup
cannot inject markup into the page.

## Design tokens

All colour, radius, shadow and font decisions live in `tailwind.config.ts`.
Components reference them by name — `bg-sauti-blue`, `rounded-card`,
`shadow-search` — so the interface can be re-themed from that single file.

```
sauti.bg          #FFFFFF     surfaces
sauti.surface     #F5F5F7     hovers, inactive fills
sauti.border      #E5E7EB     hairlines
sauti.text        #1A1A2E     primary text
sauti.textMuted   #6B7280     secondary text
sauti.textFaint   #9CA3AF     captions, placeholders
sauti.blue        #2563EB     Internet
sauti.orange      #EA580C     Business
sauti.green       #059669     Education
sauti.purple      #7C3AED     News
```

Each accent has a `…Soft` wash for card backgrounds. Radii: `card` 12px,
`large` 16px, `pill` 999px.

## Responsive behaviour

Below 768px (`md`) the sidebar is replaced by a three-tab bar pinned to the
bottom, and the content column gains bottom padding so nothing hides beneath
it. At 768px and above the sidebar becomes a fixed 240px rail and the content
column carries a matching left offset.

## Conventions

- **No `any`.** `strict` is on, along with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, so
  unchecked array access is a compile error rather than a silent `undefined`.
- **No hardcoded content in components.** Every string and list comes from
  `data/mock.ts`.
- **No inline styles.** Colour is passed as Tailwind class strings
  (`text-sauti-blue`) rather than raw hex, which keeps values inside the token
  vocabulary. Note this means Tailwind's scanner must see the class literals,
  which is why `data/` is listed in the `content` glob.
- **Primitives before markup.** Shared surfaces use `components/ui/` so radius,
  border and shadow stay consistent.

## Known limitations

- A chat turn that fails still returns HTTP 200 with a canned apology. Clients
  must read `engine_ok` or `degraded`; the status code alone does not tell you.
- Conversation history is per-browser. The backend stores transcripts but has
  no endpoint to list them, so ids are kept in `localStorage` and cleared when
  the user forgets a conversation. Clearing site data loses the list.
- Voice input depends on `MediaRecorder`, which Firefox and older Safari
  lack. The mic is disabled there rather than failing silently.
- Deleting a conversation removes only the local reference; the stored
  transcript is left on the server.
- Colours outside the `sauti.*` vocabulary remain in two places, both inherited
  from the original design: `text-amber-400` on sun and star glyphs, and
  `gray-200`/`gray-300` on image placeholders.

## Deploying to Render

`render.yaml` is a Render blueprint. Connect the repo in Render, pick
**Blueprint**, and Render reads it.

| Variable | Must set | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | yes | The frontend's public origin, e.g. `https://sauti-ai.onrender.com`. Set after the first frontend deploy. |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | yes | From [console.groq.com](https://console.groq.com/keys). |
| `SEARCH_API_KEY` | for real research | Any `SEARCH_PROVIDER` other than `stub`. |

`ADMIN_TOKEN` and `SECRET_KEY` are generated for you. Postgres is provisioned
and `DATABASE_URL` wired in automatically.

**Two things that will bite if ignored:**

1. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` must be set before the build, not after.** Next.js
   inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` into the client bundle at build time. If the variable
   is empty during `npm run build`, the deployed app is permanently hardwired to
   `http://localhost:8000`, and no runtime change fixes it — you must redeploy.
   Deploy the backend first, copy its URL, then deploy the frontend.
2. **Free-tier disks do not exist**, so uploaded media under `instance/media`
   is lost on every restart and redeploy. Uncomment the `disk` block and use a
   paid plan if you need uploads to persist.

Deploy order: backend first, then frontend with its URL.

### Deploying elsewhere

The frontend deploys as any standard Next.js application — Vercel, or any Node
host. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` to the public address of the backend and add
that origin to the backend's `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, or the browser will be blocked
by CORS.

For **Vercel**: import the repository, keep the build command as `npm run
build` and the output as the default `.next`.

For a **Node host**:

```bash
npm ci
npm run build
npm run start     # listens on $PORT, default 3000
```

The backend deploys with gunicorn. Note the target is `wsgi:app`, not
`backend.app:app` — that module only exports `create_app`, never a module-level
`app`:

```bash
gunicorn -w 2 -b 0.0.0.0:$PORT wsgi:app
```

It must run with the repository root as the working directory, because the `ai`
package is imported at request time and is not included in the installed
distribution.
